candidates.attacker_control: For FeedParser, an uploaded RSS/Atom file (or any XML stream routed to a parser that obtains its SAXParser from ParseContext/XMLReaderUtils) is attacker-controlled. For NetworkParser, the XML response from the configured parser endpoint, including a TikaCLI -c/--client network URI, is attacker-influenced if that endpoint is malicious or reached over an unauthenticated/plaintext channel. Library users can also reach the same parser-helper gap directly.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Most in-repo SAX document parsers (XMLParser, DIFParser, OOXML/XPS/ODF/WordML/Word2006ML parsers, EpubContentParser, Tesseract OCR) pass OfflineContentHandler directly as the outer parse handler, which does register it as EntityResolver and blocks external entities. TikaServer.fillMetadata forces application/xml toward HtmlParser, limiting direct XML parsing. NetworkParser is not used by the default Tika server endpoints; it is reached via TikaCLI network-client mode or programmatic use. FeedParser depends on external ROME 1.5.1 behavior that is not present in this source snapshot, so the feed path is a source-backed lead but not confirmed. FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING limits but does not disable external entity resolution.
candidates.impact: XML external entity resolution can disclose local files or internal HTTP resources into extracted text/metadata (XXE/SSRF) on the machine running Tika, and unrestricted DOCTYPE processing can enable entity-expansion/DOCTYPE-based denial of service in XML parsing paths. In a server deployment the impact depends on which XML parser path is reachable; in NetworkParser/CLI-client mode the attacker controls the parser response.
candidates.prerequisites: A reachable XML entry point: default FeedParser support for application/rss+xml or application/atom+xml (service registration files are not present in this snapshot), TikaCLI network-client mode or other programmatic NetworkParser use, or third-party/library code calling ParseContext.getSAXParser()/XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParser() without an outer OfflineContentHandler. External entity resolution requires the underlying JAXP parser to honor entities (the stock Xerces implementation does).
candidates.root_cause: Tika's central SAX helpers create parsers with only FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING. XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParser() returns a SAXParser with no entity resolver, and getSAXParserFactory() (and the duplicate in ParseContext) does not disable external general/parameter entities, external DTD loading, or DOCTYPE declarations. Security therefore depends on each caller making OfflineContentHandler the outer DefaultHandler. NetworkParser violates that assumption by passing a TeeContentHandler to SAXParser.parse; TeeContentHandler extends DefaultHandler without overriding resolveEntity, so its default null resolution is used and the nested OfflineContentHandler is never consulted. FeedParser similarly passes attacker-controlled feed XML directly to ROME without any visible entity/doctype hardening.
candidates.title: XML external entity (XXE) exposure in SAX parsing helpers and feed/network XML paths
candidates.trace: XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParser() (106-113) simply calls getSAXParserFactory().newSAXParser(); the factory (130-147) sets namespace-aware, non-validating, and FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING only. It never calls setEntityResolver or disables external-general-entities/external-parameter-entities/load-external-dtd/disallow-doctype-decl. ParseContext.getSAXParser() delegates to this helper (131-137), and its own getSAXParserFactory() (150-169) has the same limitation. In NetworkParser.ParsingTask.parse (118-130), the parser receives new TeeContentHandler(tagged, new MetaHandler(...)); tagged contains new TaggedContentHandler(new OfflineContentHandler(handler)). Because SAXParser.parse installs the outer DefaultHandler (TeeContentHandler) as the EntityResolver, TeeContentHandler inherits DefaultHandler.resolveEntity returning null, so the parser performs default external resolution and the nested OfflineContentHandler only receives content events. Any entity value/filesystem or URL response is therefore expanded into the parsed output. FeedParser.parse (64-71) builds a SyndFeedInput over the raw CloseShieldInputStream with no entity resolver or doctype restriction, so an attacker-controlled feed reaches ROME's XML parsing defaults.
candidates.unverified: ROME 1.5.1's default doctype/entity handling could not be inspected because dependency sources/JARs are not in the snapshot. META-INF/services parser registrations are absent, so default reachability of FeedParser and the exact server routing were not confirmed. NetworkParser reachability requires TikaCLI network-client mode or programmatic use rather than a default HTTP endpoint. No exploit was executed and no runtime confirmation was performed; the exact upstream fix/CVE mapping is unknown.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned 785-file Apache Tika 1.18 production snapshot. The snapshot contains main sources for tika-core, tika-parsers, tika-server, tika-app, tika-batch, tika-eval, tika-translate, tika-xmp, tika-serialization, tika-langdetect, tika-nlp, tika-dl, tika-dotnet, tika-java7, and deployment descriptors, but no test tree and no META-INF/service registration files. I concentrated on XML parsing/SAX/DOM/StAX helpers, parser entry points and handlers, tika-server resources/writers and CLI options, archive/embedded-document handling, path construction, reflection/configuration, and external-command and translator code. The leading candidate was traced from the central SAX helper through NetworkParser and the FeedParser entry point; other parser classes were checked for direct OfflineContentHandler use and mitigation. This was not an exhaustive line-by-line review of every parser or dependency.
limitations: Dependency sources/JARs (notably ROME 1.5.1, POI 3.17, PDFBox 2.0.9, commons-compress, JDOM2, and the JAXP implementation) are not present, so their default entity/doctype behavior and known vulnerabilities could not be verified from source.

The snapshot omits all META-INF/service registration files and the test tree, so which parsers are registered by default and the exact default reachability of FeedParser/NetworkParser could not be confirmed.
No build, test, scanner, or exploit execution was performed; candidate status is a source-evidence lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

The exact upstream fix commit/CVE boundary is unknown; the snapshot appears to be the 1.18 release, so multiple post-1.18 vulnerability classes (XXE, entity-expansion DoS, parser resource-exhaustion DoS) are potentially applicable and only one candidate could be submitted.
Several parser paths (CHM, DBF, WordPerfect, MP3, PST, image and PDF internals, and third-party library behavior) were reviewed only at a high level, not exhaustively.

rejected_leads.lead: ISArchiveParser builds filesystem paths from attacker-derived metadata ("Study Assay File Name") with new File(location + assayFileName) and has mutable shared location/studyFileName state
rejected_leads.reason: A local file-read/path-traversal pattern is visible, but it requires an adjacent i_*.txt investigation file matching the study name and is primarily a local-directory/CLI scenario. The parser's default registration is not visible in the snapshot, so it was not selected as the strongest candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: ICNSParser uses file-controlled image_length directly for byte[] allocation and indexed reads without bounds checks; BPGParser allocates byte[xmpLength] from file data
rejected_leads.reason: These are source-evident denial-of-service/robustness issues (negative/oversized allocation, out-of-bounds access), but impact is lower than the XML external entity lead and no confidentiality/integrity effect was established.

rejected_leads.lead: UnpackerResource and RecursiveMetadataResource accumulate all embedded resources/content in memory without an obvious size/resource cap
rejected_leads.reason: Generic resource-exhaustion DoS, but the server is intentionally an extraction service and no specific parser flaw was established; lower confidence and impact than the XXE lead.
It is explicitly opt-in, requires both --enableFileUrl and --enableUnsecureFeatures, and is documented as equivalent to CVE-2015-3271; this is intentional behavior rather than a bypass.

rejected_leads.lead: TikaCLI -z/FileEmbeddedDocumentExtractor writes embedded files using metadata names and extractDir
rejected_leads.reason: The code applies Commons IO FilenameUtils.normalize and Java File(parent, child) resolution; no confirmed traversal bypass was established, and this is a local CLI workflow.

rejected_leads.lead: TikaServer X-Tika-OCR/X-Tika-PDF header reflection and Tesseract/ImageMagick path setting
rejected_leads.reason: checkTrustWorthy limits values to an allowlist, ProcessBuilder passes argument arrays rather than a shell command, and the path setters append fixed executable names; no confirmed command injection or RCE was found.

rejected_leads.lead: ZipWriter/TarWriter put attacker-derived embedded resource names into returned archives
rejected_leads.reason: This is client-side archive extraction (zip-slip against a downstream extractor), not a server-side file write; no direct Tika server compromise was established.

rejected_leads.lead: PDF actions/embedded file specs and Jackcess linked-database resolution
rejected_leads.reason: PDF actions are extraction-only and off by default, and Jackcess explicitly installs an IgnoreLinkResolver that throws rather than opening linked databases; no actionable bypass was found.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Tika 1.18 production source snapshot (785 visible files; tests and META-INF service registrations are absent). The strongest lead is unhardened XML external-entity handling in the SAX parsing infrastructure: XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParser()/getSAXParserFactory() enable only FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and do not install an ignoring EntityResolver or disable external entities/DOCTYPEs. Most in-repo parsers compensate by wrapping their handler directly in OfflineContentHandler, but NetworkParser passes a TeeContentHandler as the actual DefaultHandler, so its nested OfflineContentHandler is never registered as the parser's EntityResolver and external entities are resolved. FeedParser is a further unverified XML entry point that passes attacker XML to ROME without any visible doctype/entity restriction. No code was executed and no runtime confirmation is claimed.
